messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (gateway). Error rate 15% over 5m, region: us-west-2. Paging oncall.

oncall-liz: on it. jumping in. can you paste the initial metric graph? :eyes:

sre-ben: attaching quick tail of gateway logs, small sample: 
```
2026-03-10T14:01:58Z gateway-01 ERROR request_id=abc123 backend=runner-3 status=502 message=upstream reset
2026-03-10T14:02:12Z runner-3 CRITICAL pid=12345 sig=11 reason=segfault module=quant_attention.so
2026-03-10T14:02:14Z gateway-02 ERROR request_id=def456 backend=runner-4 status=504 message=timeout
```

runtime-nora: I see repeated segfaults on runner-3 and OOM-ish traces on runner-7. KV cache growth looks suspect. Increasing OOM counters.

eng-miguel: copying model-runner logs: 
```
[14:02:12] model-runner[12345]: Fatal signal 11 at 0x7f8b2a3c
[14:02:12] stack: quant_attention+0x4f2
[14:02:12] memory: RSS spike from 6.2G -> 14.1G in 3s
```

oncall-liz: is this isolated to a single model variant? any correlation with quantized kernels?

sre-ben: correlating — yes, most crashes map to the int8-quant variants (v1.2.3-q8). fallback (fp16) instances are stable.

runtime-nora: mitigation plan: 1) route new traffic away from runner pool 3 & 7, 2) enable automatic fallback to fp16 variant for gateway routing, 3) cordon problematic nodes and drain, 4) hotpatch quant kernel if needed.

eng-miguel: executing routing change now: 
```
# move traffic -> fp16-variant for model: redwood/bison-13b
redwoodctl route set --model bison-13b --variant fp16 --weight 100 --region us-west-2
```

incident-bot: change deployed — routing update accepted by control-plane (req id dfd-987).

support-jaya: customer-impact check: telemetry shows ~8% of hosted API requests in us-west-2 failed with 5xx during the spike window. Flagging top 3 customers for outreach; creating C-9212.

product-sam: note — a few PLG customers reported chat sessions dropping. marking as P1 potential customer-impact.

oncall-liz: running node cordon/drain commands: 
```
kubectl cordon node-10.usw2 && kubectl drain node-10.usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
systemctl restart model-runner.service on node-11
```

runtime-nora: node-10 drained, runner pods rescheduled. starting gradual traffic restore to region once 5m error rate <1%.

eng-miguel: quick workaround patch ready. builds: quant-kernel v1.2.4 -> adds bounds check on KV cache. want me to roll to staging then canary to 10%?

sre-ben: prefer rolling routing fallback until patch validated. low-risk: keep routing to fp16 for next 30m, then canary.

support-jaya: alerted affected accounts via status page and opened proactive tickets. email template sent.

product-sam: ETA on customer-facing update?

oncall-liz: I'll post an interim status in 10m after we observe metrics. handing off to eng-miguel for the hotpatch. if things re-escalate ping @oncall-liz.

eng-miguel: taking over for the hotpatch. will push to staging now, will report back.

incident-bot: Note: incident channel auto-log created: incident-1769112222.

product-sam: please capture rollback criteria in the ticket: increased 5xx on fp16 variant, or elevated latency >200ms p95.

eng-miguel: staging patch passed smoke. scheduling canary to 10% at 14:20 UTC.

sre-ben: monitoring: error rate dropped to 0.9% after routing change. latency stable. continuing observation.

oncall-liz: thanks all — holding the page. will update in 30m with an incident summary and owners for postmortem. :thumbsup:

support-jaya: C-9212 created, outreach started. will keep customers updated.

eng-miguel: canary looks good at 10%. promoting to 50% in 5m.

runtime-nora: KV cache caps will be added to our long term fix. noted for postmortem.

oncall-liz: last update: error rates normalized after routing + drain + canary. handing off to eng-miguel & runtime-nora for hotpatch rollout and postmortem. incident status: mitigated.

product-sam: assigned postmortem leads: eng-miguel (fix), runtime-nora (runtime mitigations), support-jaya (customer comms).

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Close when postmortem doc and timeline posted.
